claim.statement: The primary paper cited by M-CSA M0219 proposal 2 explicitly starts its QM/MM model from human transketolase structure 4KXV. The preserved structure maps its P29401-derived chain-A construct and author Lys244/His258 to P29401 sequence positions 244/258. This resolves the model-template protein and two residue identities; it does not establish the proposed catalytic roles or experimental applicability of the complete mechanism.

evidence.citation: Luedtke et al. (2013), PDB 4KXV; DOI 10.2210/pdb4KXV/pdb; PMID 23965678. PDB archive data: CC0 1.0.
evidence.experimental_context: Current revision 2.1 (2023-09-20), human-derived TKT expressed in E. coli. The deposited alignment maps chain-A author/label positions 1-623 to P29401 1-623; Lys244 and His258 retain those positions. The trailing 14 residues are an expression tag. No physiological metal or catalytic protonation is inferred.

evidence.citation: Prejano, Medina, Ramos, Russo, Fernandes and Marino (2020), ACS Catalysis 10, 2872-2881; DOI 10.1021/acscatal.9b04690; PMID 33828899. Preserved BioC text: CC BY 4.0.
evidence.experimental_context: The methods explicitly identify a QM/MM model derived from human 4KXV and name Lys244A/His258A. Direct support is limited to the reported model-template and residue context. Catalytic roles/protonation are computational, informed by cited yeast experiments. The local prior download has no original HTTP receipt, as disclosed in the inventory.

evidence.citation: PDBe official UniProt mapping for 4KXV, retrieved 2026-09-06.
evidence.experimental_context: The official mapping exposes entity 1/chain A/struct asym A as P29401 positions 1-623 with identity 1.0. This is a second representation of the same deposit, not independent experimental evidence.

evidence.citation: PDBe official residue listing for 4KXV, retrieved 2026-09-06.
evidence.experimental_context: Entity 1/chain A/struct asym A lists LYS author/label 244 and HIS author/label 258 with observed_ratio 1.0. This supports residue presence and numbering only.

evidence.citation: wwPDB versioned archive, 4KXV revision 1.3 (2019-09-04); DOI 10.2210/pdb4KXV/pdb. PDB archive data: CC0 1.0.
evidence.experimental_context: The archived pre-publication entry maps chain-A author/label Lys244 and His258 to P29401 244 and 258, agreeing with current revision 2.1. Archive provenance corroborates numbering across revisions; it does not establish the exact coordinate file used in the computation.

limits.statement: The paper cites prior yeast mutagenesis and kinetics to motivate the human His258A-Lys244A dyad and models its catalytic roles. Protein and residue identity do not establish those roles experimentally.
The neutral Lys244A assignment and reported pKa 3.99 are computational choices/predictions; this annotation does not infer protonation from residue identity or the deposited structure.

The cited paper investigates the first catalytic stage with QM/MM; a prior cluster model supplies its broader cycle. No full source trajectory, atom-mapped bond edits, or proposal-wide experimental applicability is validated.

Proposal-2 prose and the paper describe X5P + E4P to G3P + F6P. The sugar-derived components have carbon counts consistent with that context, while all six raw proposal-2 MRVs retain conflicting CHEBI:57483 (S7P) labels on sugar atoms. This does not establish exact structures, stereochemistry, or speciation. Those source labels and the distinct entry-level reaction are preserved; no exact chemical normalization or entry-reaction/proposal equivalence is asserted.
Proposal 1 retains its yeast P23254/1TRK context. This human model-template mapping does not transfer proposal-1 residue roles to P29401 or merge the alternatives.

Archived 4KXV v1.3 and current v2.1 both contain P29401 residues 1-623 followed by a 14-residue expression tag and map Lys244/His258 identically. A major atomic-model revision followed the paper; neither archive provenance nor the citation establishes the exact coordinate bytes used for the computation.
The structure/model context does not resolve one physiological divalent-metal identity for human transketolase.

chemical_observations.source_description: The current 2QUT deposit contains four modeled nonpolymer 13P instances.
The generic deposited 13P component dictionary records C2-O2 value_order doub.
The 2QUT structure title designates a dihydroxyacetone phosphate enamine intermediate in rabbit-muscle fructose-bisphosphate aldolase.
All four modeled deposited 13P instances omit dictionary atom O2.
The primary abstract describes trapping of the enamine intermediate at Lys229 in the authors' native aldolase context.

chemical_reconciliation.statement: The generic 13P dictionary C2-O2 doub record, modeled O2 omission, four Lys-NZ to 13P-C2 connections with unknown value_order, and paper/deposit enamine descriptions remain separate source facts; no exact bound bond order or protonation is assigned.

claim.statement: Current 2QUT deposit bytes record four 13P nonpolymer instances, each covalently connected from C2 to a chain-specific Lys229 NZ, and designate the state as a DHAP enamine intermediate; the paper abstract separately describes trapping an enamine at Lys229 in the authors' native aldolase context. Generic-dictionary C2-O2 doub, modeled O2 omission, and unknown deposited connection order are retained without chemical normalization. This typed context refines the retained m0222.2qut.dhap-derived-covalent-moiety observation and is not independent supporting evidence.

limits.statement: The four deposited covalent rows carry source_bond_order_code null and the raw unknown token ?; no exact protein-moiety bond order is assigned.
No exact free ChEBI identity, bound protonation, or unsourced normalized chemical identity is assigned.
Generic 13P dictionary C2-O2 doub, modeled O2 omission, and Lys-C2 connection rows are retained as distinct source scopes and remain chemically unreconciled.
The retained 2QUT CIF is revision 1.3 from 2024 and is not asserted to be the exact coordinate or dictionary representation used for the 2007 publication.
This typed context refines the retained m0222.2qut.dhap-derived-covalent-moiety observation from the same 2QUT source and is not independent supporting evidence.
The record-level structure context does not close a balanced exact reaction instance or physiological direction.
The observation does not validate M-CSA Step 1, the complete proposal, or the archaeal narrative.
The paper's native-enzyme wording is retained only for its comparator construct and is not a generic validated-native or physiological-state label.
The new typed attachment rows do not assert canonical protein residue mapping; the current-deposit author229-to-P00883-230 correspondence remains audit evidence and an unchanged legacy-v1 claim.
No temporal trajectory, free-DHAP attack, atom-mapped transition, proton transfer, or trapping preparation is observed by this annotation.

claim.statement: Rabbit ALDOA structure 2QUT supports a DHAP-derived covalent moiety at chain-A author Lys229, mapped to P00883 Lys230. The deposit and primary publication assign an enamine intermediate. This provides direct structural counterevidence to the G3P identity in M-CSA Step 1 prose and supports DHAP as the parent moiety of the captured rabbit Lys adduct; it does not resolve the Step 1 attack trajectory.

evidence.citation: St-Jean and Sygusch (2007), PDB 2QUT; DOI 10.2210/pdb2QUT/pdb; PMID 17728250. PDB archive data: CC0 1.0.
evidence.experimental_context: The preserved mmCIF records chain-A Lys229 NZ linked to ligand 13P C2, a P00883 alignment offset of one residue, and an enamine title. Its mutation field is unspecified; the native assignment comes from the cited paper and RCSB entry page.
The accessible abstract assigns the trapped DHAP-derived enamine at Lys229 to native aldolase and distinguishes the Lys146Met iminium context. Article body is not redistributed.

evidence.citation: Choi et al. (2001), PDB 1J4E; DOI 10.2210/pdb1J4E/pdb; PMID 11705376.
evidence.experimental_context: Four-Cys engineered construct with a reduced DHAP-derived covalent trap. The paper reports NaBH4 trapping in the presence of FBP. This is not a direct observation of a native Schiff base, iminium, or free-DHAP attack; its legacy sequence mapping is not used here.

The accessible abstract identifies the DHAP-derived Schiff-base precursor and chemical trapping conditions; the deposited reduced trap remains distinct from the 2QUT enamine. Article body is not redistributed.

limits.statement: The structures do not directly observe the complete M-CSA Step 1 attack trajectory, temporal ordering, or condensation from free DHAP. Source arrow annotations remain unvalidated as atom-mapped bond edits.
This rabbit-site observation does not assign the entire mixed rabbit/archaeal proposal or the archaeal Step 10 narrative to P00883.
The DHAP-derived covalent moiety is not assigned an exact free-metabolite ChEBI identifier. M-CSA CHEBI:57642 remains a source label; exact bound protonation and bond order remain unasserted.

The preserved M-CSA Step 1 prose names G3P while its drawing labels DHAP; Step 7 prose names incoming glycerone phosphate while the drawing labels incoming G3P. The primary evidence supports the DHAP-derived covalent moiety, without silently rewriting either source field.
